f07_confirmation.caption: LOCAL/SIMPLE effects in 12 paired A5000 time blocks. Left: lines connect the same block's two fixed 32B histories (one root; C4 on, P4 off, frozen proposals; verification through commit). Noncrossing is primary; crossing and their ratio-of-ratios interaction are supporting. Right: the separately analyzed 8B target-only primary endpoint weights two fixed conversations equally in log time, from response through reset. Positive $100(1-\mathrm{LOCAL}/\mathrm{SIMPLE})\%$ means less LOCAL time. Printed limits give individual 95\% joint whole-block intervals. The interaction has null value one.
f07_confirmation.description: Two panels show all twelve numbered time blocks. Lines connect cases within each block. The 32B crossing effects consistently favor LOCAL, while the primary noncrossing interval spans zero. The separately clocked 8B target-only panel retains both conversations and their equal-weight diamond; its primary interval also spans zero. Printed intervals accompany the estimates, and the supporting ratio-of-ratios interaction is below one.

f04_few_column.caption: RTX resident-request controls with SIMPLE fixed and P4 off (reset through final synchronization). Dots show 24 root effects per contrast; diamonds and bars give equal-root/equal-block geometric reductions and individual 95\% crossed stratified-root/whole-block intervals. C1/B is the sole primary contrast; C4 contrasts are descriptive. Positive values mean time saved. The waterfall instead reports arithmetic mean milliseconds saved, B minus C1; it does not decompose the geometric effects.
f04_few_column.description: A dispatch matrix distinguishes scalar loop B, grouped scalar C1 and few-column C4. Each contrast retains twelve code and twelve math root effects plus its geometric summary. The primary C1/B interval crosses zero; both descriptive C4 intervals favor the candidate. A separate arithmetic waterfall shows verification savings outweighed by prefill cost, ending at a net cost of 80.52 milliseconds. All signed values and the zero lines remain visible.

f05_prefill.caption: Independent A5000 and RTX P4 controls with SIMPLE fixed (resident requests, reset through final synchronization). The studies contain 12 and 24 roots, each reused in three contrasts (36 study-specific roots; 108 effect marks). Horizontal positions follow prompt-length rank, not proportional token spacing; the studies are unpaired. Row labels specify candidate/control; positive reductions mean less candidate time. Diamonds and bars give equal-root geometric reductions and individual 95\% code/math-stratified root intervals. The outlined A5000 \texttt{train/279} effect is $-0.33\%$.
f05_prefill.description: Three contrast rows appear in two independent deployment columns. Every root effect is retained at a rank ordered by prompt length, with a separate overall diamond and confidence interval. Packing favors the candidate for every root in the first two rows. At fixed P4, the A5000 train/279 point is an outlined diamond at a small negative reduction; it is not moved to zero. The two studies are not paired.

f03_alternate.caption: Native SIMPLE and LOCAL times for all 48 A5000 confirmation pairs in 12 time blocks. Each stem links the two arms of one fixed case in one block. The two 32B histories use verification-through-commit milliseconds with C4 on, P4 off and frozen proposals; the two fixed 8B target-only conversations use seconds for two-turn response plus reset. Summary reductions use paired time ratios and individual 95\% whole-block intervals. Noncrossing and equal-conversation service are primary for their respective clocks. The supporting 32B interaction is the crossing/noncrossing ratio of ratios, with null value one.
f03_alternate.description: Four plots expose every native pair against block index. The 32B crossing shows a consistent gap between the two arm times, unlike the noncrossing history. Both separate 8B conversations retain blocks with either arm faster. Individual intervals accompany the two primary endpoints and the supporting comparisons.

f05_prompt_length.caption: Diagnostic view of the three direct resident-request contrasts in two independent studies, with SIMPLE fixed and clocks from reset through final synchronization. The horizontal axis uses observed prompt tokens within each study; it is not a between-deployment comparison or a fitted causal trend. All 108 effect marks represent 36 study-specific root entries recurring across three contrasts. Candidate/control reductions are positive when the candidate takes less time. Squares and bars give equal-root geometric estimates and individual 95\% code/math-stratified root intervals. The open A5000 \texttt{train/279} diamond retains its negative effect at fixed P4.
f05_prompt_length.description: Six panels place the original root effects at their measured prompt lengths. Equal prompt lengths can overlap; no curve is fitted. Each panel retains its separate overall square and confidence interval. The longest A5000 prompt, train/279, is an open diamond slightly below zero under speculation at fixed P4. This is a diagnostic alternative to the selected rank plot.
